region.text: the land of the Allahabad Pillar tributaries, Rajasthan, the Punjab and Sind plus the Eastern Kushan frontier, that the dossier's own 380 vassal_end draws as direct Gupta land (region of gupta-empire ledger/11)

events.note: c. 380: Chandragupta II, crowned c. 380 (infobox), is 'directly controlling a vast territory which stretched from the Oxus River in the west to the Bengal region in the east' (Chandragupta II page). The dossier's own ledger/11 ends the tribute of the Rajasthan, Punjab and Sind land in 380 and draws it direct, but the compiler leaves a vassal_end's land to nobody, so 2,245 cells were unowned from 380 to 382 until the 383 keyframe snap; this gain draws them as Gupta land from 380 as the dossier intends.

region.text: Kucha, between Aksu to the west and Karasahr to the east (the dossier's own keyframe region)

events.note: Kucha has its own listed kings in this period ('Bai Shan 280', 'Long Hui 326', 'Bai Chun 349', 'Bai Zhen 382' on the Kucha page) and was conquered by Lu Guang only in 383 ('Lu Guang obtained the surrender of Karashar and conquered Kucha in 383 CE'), yet the compiled map gives its keyframe land to the Western Regions colony from -60 on (R1) and Kucha owns no cell at any anchor from 100 on. The protectorate page has no protectorate between the Han and its revival 'in 335 by Former Liang', the year the protectorate's own ledger/16 takes Kucha, so Kucha is drawn independent from 300 until then. [Review p0300-p0399, 2 Nov 2026: Kucha keeps its land from 300 but is drawn as a Western Jin vassal until 327 (events/3, events/4): the Chief Official of the Western Regions page has the office 're-established and maintained by the Cao Wei and the Western Jin until around 328', and the western-jin dossier draws the rest of the Tarim as its vassal tint to 328 on that page; independent 328-334.]

region.text: Chang'an, recaptured for the Jin by Jia Ya in 312

Added by the reviewer with keyframe_overrides/0, which cuts the city from the Jin's 311 shape.

keyframe_overrides.why: For 311-312. The dossiers of cheng-han and former-zhao cut these lands out of Cliopatria's Cheng Han and Former Zhao shapes because the pages put them under Jin, but this Jin keyframe is Cliopatria's shape as drawn, which lacks them, so they were nobody's. Han-Zhao page: 'Emperor Min being installed at Chang'an in 312', 'Liu Yao captured Chang'an in 316, ending the Western Jin dynasty'. Li Xiong page: 'he made no serious attempts to capture Jin's Ning Province' (Yunnan and Guizhou), taken by Li Shou only in 333. Hanzhong, also cut from the Cheng shape (Cheng's only from 314), is left as it is: the Cheng-Han page does not say who held it before 314. [Review p0300-p0399, 2 Nov 2026: Chang'an cut from this 311 shape. Emperor Min of Jin page: in 311 Prince Ye fled after the fall of Luoyang, and 'Jia was able to capture Chang'an in 312, allowing Prince Ye to enter and set up his headquarters there', so the city was not Jin's at the end of 311; events/2 gives it back to the Jin in 312. The page does not say who held it in 311, so it is left to nobody for that year.]
